questions.questionText: hour 15 minutes Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. DO NOT WRITE IN ANY BARCODES. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.

The diagram shows the marginal private benefit (MPB), the marginal private cost (MPC) and the marginal social cost (MSC) for firms in an industry. The equilibrium price is point X. price MSC MPC X MPB = MSB O quantity What should happen to achieve allocative efficiency?

options.A: a decrease in consumption and an increase in price
options.B: a decrease in production and no change in price
options.C: an increase in consumption and a decrease in production
options.D: an increase in price and no change in production

questions.questionText: In deciding whether to invest in a new project, what would be taken into account in government cost-benefit analysis but not by a private company?

options.A: consultancy fees
options.B: consumer surplus
options.C: interest charges
options.D: tax payments

questions.questionText: What is not held constant when calculating the income effect of a change in the price of a good?

options.A: the consumer’s money income
options.B: the consumer’s preferences
options.C: the consumer’s real income
options.D: the prices of other goods

Firms X, Y and Z are profit maximising private firms. X operates in a perfectly competitive industry, Y in a monopolistically competitive industry and Z is a single monopolist. Which statement is correct?

options.A: Only X satisfies the condition for allocative efficiency.
options.B: Only X faces no barriers to entry in the long run.
options.C: Only Y and Z can make a supernormal profit in the long run.
options.D: Only Z has a product differentiation.

questions.questionText: What are the correct formulae for calculating average cost (AC) and average revenue (AR)? AC AR TC TR

options.A: key MC MR MC = marginal cost TC
options.B: P × Q MR = marginal revenue P P = price TC P × Q C Q = quantity Q Q TC = total cost TC TR D TR = total revenue Q P

questions.questionText: A Hawker Centre where there are many outdoor stalls is a popular and cheap place to eat in Singapore. They sell a large variety of food but many sell the same dishes cooked in different ways. The cost of setting up a stall is low and prices charged are very similar. Of which market structure is this an example?

options.A: monopolistic competition
options.B: monopoly
options.C: oligopoly
options.D: perfect competition

questions.questionText: What is an example of horizontal integration?

options.A: A bank takes over a travel agent.
options.B: A car manufacturer buys a component supplier.
options.C: A cotton mill doubles its output of existing products.
options.D: Two breweries merge.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows a firm that is a sales revenue maximiser. total costs $ total revenue O R S T output What is correct for this firm?

options.A: Output takes place at R and price is at its highest.
options.B: Output takes place at S and profits are maximised.
options.C: Output takes place at T and price is equal to the profit maximising price.
options.D: Output takes place at T and price is lower than the profit maximising price.

questions.questionText: What is an essential feature of the principal-agent problem?

options.A: the aim of the firm is profit maximisation
options.B: the need for co-operation between firms in the same industry
options.C: the separation of ownership and control
options.D: the uncertainty about a rival competitor’s pricing policy

questions.questionText: Which characteristic of an industry works towards reducing the barriers to entry for new firms?

options.A: significant advertising expenditure by existing firms
options.B: significant economies of scale
options.C: the absence of large costs associated with investment in capital assets
options.D: the possession by existing firms of product and process patents

questions.questionText: The government wishes to increase the use of a service with positive externalities. Which policy measure is most likely to produce the desired outcome?

options.A: decreasing income tax
options.B: increasing transfer payments to the consumer
options.C: leaving the provision of the service to the private sector
options.D: subsidising the producers of the service

questions.questionText: The government imposes a maximum wage limit on recording artists. What must result in the short-run if the measure is effective?

options.A: a decrease in the demand for recording artists
options.B: a decrease in the economic rent earned by recording artists
options.C: a decrease in the profits of record companies
options.D: a decrease in the supply of recording artists

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the market for labour in an industry in the short-run. S wages R W D O Q quantity of labour What does the area OWRQ represent?

options.A: consumers’ surplus
options.B: economic rent
options.C: the opportunity cost of labour
options.D: transfer earnings

questions.questionText: A country introduces a national minimum wage (NMW) of $10 per hour. In which industry is the NMW likely to cause the most unemployment? equilibrium wage rate wage elasticity of wage elasticity of before NMW ($ per hour) demand for labour supply of labour
Economics textbooks state that for a firm in imperfect competition labour is a derived demand. How is the demand curve for labour derived?

options.A: by multiplying the average physical product by the average revenue
options.B: by multiplying the average physical product by the marginal revenue
options.C: by multiplying the marginal physical product by the marginal cost
options.D: by multiplying the marginal physical product by the marginal revenue

questions.questionText: The diagram shows changes in the numbers employed in four different industries in a city between 2012 and 2017. employment finance (000s) 50 manufacturing education leisure 2012 2013 2014 2015 2016 2017 What can be concluded from the diagram?

options.A: Finance was always the largest employer.
options.B: Leisure had the fastest growth rate in employment.
options.C: Manufacturing was the only industry to show signs of decline.
options.D: Total employment in the four industries decreased over the period.

questions.questionText: What is likely to make the national income of a country less reliable as an indicator of the standard of living?

options.A: a decline in the numbers engaged in subsistence farming
options.B: an increase in negative externalities
options.C: an increase in the employment of domestic servants
options.D: an increase in the numbers eating restaurant meals rather than home-cooked meals

questions.questionText: What is not included as a weighted indicator of poverty in the Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI)?

options.A: cooking fuel
options.B: electricity
options.C: medication
options.D: water

questions.questionText: What term is given to short-term unemployment when people are changing jobs?

options.A: cyclical
options.B: frictional
options.C: seasonal
options.D: voluntary

questions.questionText: Why might GDP remain unchanged despite a rise in labour productivity?

options.A: an increase in the birth rate
options.B: an increase in the population of working age
options.C: a reduction in the number of unemployed people
options.D: a reduction in the retirement age

questions.questionText: When is an increase in national income most likely to induce an increase in investment spending?

options.A: when firms have spare production capacity
options.B: when firms use labour intensive production
options.C: when the increase in income is regarded as permanent
options.D: when the increase in income is regarded as temporary

In a closed economy with no government C = 40 + 0.7 Y and I = 50, where C is consumption, Y is income and I is investment. What is the equilibrium level of income?
An increase in the money supply leaves the price level unchanged. What could explain this?

options.A: a fall in the level of employment
options.B: a fall in the level of real output
options.C: a fall in the velocity of circulation
options.D: a fall in the volume of transactions

questions.questionText: The table shows the elasticity of demand for money and the elasticity of demand for investment with respect to a change in the interest rate for four countries. Which country is closest to a Keynesian model of the economy? elasticity of demand for elasticity of demand for money with respect to investment with respect a low interest rate to any interest rate

options.A: elastic elastic
options.B: elastic relatively inelastic
options.C: inelastic elastic
options.D: inelastic relatively inelastic

questions.questionText: When making comparisons of living standards between different countries, what is not a reason why they may be misleading?

options.A: Different countries have different amounts of unrecorded economic activity.
options.B: Different countries have different rates of economic growth.
options.C: Less developed countries have limited resources to calculate accurate estimates.
options.D: There are different rates of inflation between countries.

questions.questionText: The table shows the annual rate of inflation (consumer prices) and the annual rate of unemployment for five countries in a recent year. rate of rate of inflation % unemployment % Japan Greece Content removed due to copyright restrictions USA South Africa Brazil What conclusion can be made about the relationship between inflation and unemployment?

options.A: Higher inflation is always correlated with higher unemployment.
options.B: Higher inflation is always correlated with lower unemployment.
options.C: Lower inflation is always correlated with higher unemployment.
options.D: No consistent correlation can be established.

options.A: devalue the currency
options.B: reduce direct taxes
options.C: increase the money supply
